questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using Linearity Properties
questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (F-G)$ at the point $(0,2,1)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=\operatorname{ln}⁡z\,i+xy\,k,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=-i+2z\,j-x\,k.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-G) & =∇\times F-∇\times G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡z & 0 & xy\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(0)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡z)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(0)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡z)]k \\  & =(x-0)i-(y-\frac{1}{z})j+(0-0)k \\  & =x\,i+(\frac{1}{z}-y)j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-G) & =∇\times F-∇\times G \\  & =x\,i+(\frac{1}{z}-y)j-[-i+2z\,j-x\,k] \\  & =x\,i+(\frac{1}{z}-y)j+i-2z\,j+x\,k \\  & =(x+1)\,i+(\frac{1}{z}-y-2z)j+x\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,2,1),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F-G))(0,2,1) & =(0+1)\,i+(\frac{1}{1}-2-2(1))j+0\,k \\  & =i-3\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using Linearity Properties
questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (F+G)$ at the point $(4,3,-1)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=-3\,i+z\,j+8\sqrt{x}\,\text{k},\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=-i-j.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ -3 & z & 8\sqrt{x}\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(8\sqrt{x})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(z)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(8\sqrt{x})-\frac{∂}{∂z}(-3)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(z)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(-3)]k \\  & =(0-1)i-(\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}-0)j+(0-0)k \\  & =-i-\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F+G) & =∇\times F+∇\times G \\  & =-i-\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\,j+[-i-j] \\  & =-i-\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\,j-i-j \\  & =-2\,i-(\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}+1)j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(4,3,-1),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\times (F+G))(4,3,-1) & =-2\,i-(\frac{4}{\sqrt{4}}+1)j \\  & =-2\,i-3\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using the Product Rule
questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨yz,0,-{z}^{2}⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=xy-z.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨0,y,-z⟩,\,∇f=⟨y,x,-1⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(0,-1,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ y & x & -1 \\ yz & 0 & -{z}^{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =[x(-{z}^{2})-(-1)(0)]i-[y(-{z}^{2})-(-1)(yz)]j+[y(0)-x(yz)]k \\  & =-x{z}^{2}\,i+(y{z}^{2}-yz)\,j-xyz\,k \\  & =⟨-x{z}^{2},y{z}^{2}-yz,-xyz⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(xy-z)⟨0,y,-z⟩+⟨-x{z}^{2},y{z}^{2}-yz,-xyz⟩ \\  & =⟨0,x{y}^{2}-yz,{z}^{2}-xyz⟩+⟨-x{z}^{2},y{z}^{2}-yz,-xyz⟩ \\  & =⟨-x{z}^{2},x{y}^{2}+y{z}^{2}-2yz,{z}^{2}-2xyz⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(0,-1,1) & =⟨-(0)(1)^{2},0(-1)^{2}+(-1)(1)^{2}-2(-1)(1),(1)^{2}-2(0)(-1)(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,1,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using the Product Rule
questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z,0,\operatorname{ln}⁡x⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)={e}^{2x}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨0,1-\frac{1}{x},0⟩,\,∇f=⟨2{e}^{2x},0,0⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(1,1,-4).$
questions.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2{e}^{2x} & 0 & 0 \\ z & 0 & \operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}| \\  & =[0(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)-0(0)]i-[2{e}^{2x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)-0(z)]j+[2{e}^{2x}(0)-0(z)]k \\  & =0\,i-2{e}^{2x}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,j+0\,k \\  & =⟨0,-2{e}^{2x}\operatorname{ln}⁡x,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & ={e}^{2x}⟨0,1-\frac{1}{x},0⟩+⟨0,-2{e}^{2x}\operatorname{ln}⁡x,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,{e}^{2x}-\frac{{e}^{2x}}{x},0⟩+⟨0,-2{e}^{2x}\operatorname{ln}⁡x,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,{e}^{2x}-\frac{{e}^{2x}}{x}-2{e}^{2x}\operatorname{ln}⁡x,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,{e}^{2x}(1-\frac{1}{x}-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x),0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(1,1,-4) & =⟨0,{e}^{2(1)}(1-\frac{1}{(1)}-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)),0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using Linearity Properties
questions.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (2F+G)$ at the point $(-1,1,4)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=2\sqrt{y}\,i+z\,j+yz\,k,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=x\,i-y\,j+\,k.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (2F+G) & =∇\times (2G)+∇\times G \\  & =2∇\times F+∇\times G\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ 2\sqrt{y} & z & yz\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(yz)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(z)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(yz)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(2\sqrt{y})]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(z)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\sqrt{y})]k \\  & =(z-1)i-(0-0)j+(0-\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}})k \\  & =(z-1)\,i-\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (2F+G) & =2∇\times F+∇\times G \\  & =2[(z-1)\,i-\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}}\,k]+x\,i-y\,j+\,k \\  & =(x+2z-2)\,i-y\,j+(1-\frac{2}{\sqrt{y}})\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(-1,1,4),$ we get

$$
(∇\times (2F+G))(-1,1,4)=5\,i-\,j-\,k
$$
